title: Joe Oliver as a butler on Second and Magazine
summary: She worked as house girl where Joe Oliver was a butler, and describes his leaving with a band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Oh yeah. I never did know Joe Olive. I was too young. Oh yeah. I met his wife.
Joe Olive was here. He used to work on Second and Magazine. He was a butler, I was a house girl up there.

Right there with him. He had one bad eye. I don't know if it was out, but it was swole out. You know, big eye they used to call him. And them wifey was crazy about him. He left from here. When music got good or waste, he had went away with a band somewhere and things was good there. And he left here. And I was still working for them people. And a long while after, they moved away to California. They would show people anyway. It's dangerous, but they would show people they'd be gone in a certain part of the year. So they left there too. I don't know where they would come back. What was their name? They were named Cushions or something like that. A man, his wife, and two sons. Well, one of the sons learned to play music under Joe. He used to be around with all the colored people learning music. He went to the school to learn, but he'd be with them to learn too. The big house is right on the corner of Second and Magazine. They must have had some money. Oh yeah, they did. Well, they took up that house, took up half of that square. They had a great big lawn. And then the next house sat on the corner of Third Magazine. That was rich people too. They all left eventually from out there.
